format: vaultody signed API responses, wire format v1
warning: TEST-ONLY KEYS. Every private key in this file is public. Never use them outside tests.
regeneration: Generated by the API gateway's own vector generator, which is not public. ECDSA root signatures are randomised: one already in the file is kept while its case certifies the same text, a new or changed certificate gets a fresh one, so compare verdicts and never expect a root signature to be reproduced. Keys and everything else are deterministic.

wire.cert:
"vaultody-response-key-v1
" rootId "
" base64(pub32) "
" keyId "
" notBefore "
" notAfter (ASCII, no trailing newline)
wire.rootId: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the root public key SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER (64 characters)
wire.keyId: lowercase hex of the first 16 bytes of SHA-256(pub32) (32 characters)
wire.rootSignature: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over the CERT bytes, DER encoded
wire.message:
"vaultody-response-v1
" ts "
" status "
" method "
" path "
" query "
" bodyHash "
" requestSign "
" keypairSign "
" followed by the raw response body bytes
wire.fields: path as sent (percent-encoding untouched, no query); query as sent without "?", empty if none; bodyHash = lowercase hex SHA-256 of the request body bytes as sent (before Content-Encoding), or "unread" when the gateway did not read it; requestSign = the x-api-sign request header, empty if none; keypairSign = the x-api-keypair-sign request header, empty if none. Both are printable ASCII (0x20-0x7E). Base64 is standard with padding everywhere. Decimals have no sign, no leading zero and are at most 9007199254740991.

order: All four headers present (names case-insensitive) and non-empty, else missing.
x-api-response-cert is two canonical base64 parts joined by "."; the CERT bytes are ASCII; CERT line 1 is the tag and line 2 is 64 lowercase hex, else invalid.
Line 2 (rootId) equals the rootId of a pinned root, else unknown_root.
The root signature verifies over the CERT bytes with that root, else invalid.

CERT is canonical: exactly 6 lines, printable ASCII, public key canonical base64 of 32 bytes, keyId equals the first 32 hex characters of SHA-256(public key), notBefore and notAfter canonical decimals; and notAfter - notBefore <= maxCertificateLifetimeSeconds (3600), else invalid.
x-api-response-timestamp is a canonical decimal, else invalid.
notBefore <= ts <= notAfter and now <= notAfter + skewSeconds, else expired.
x-api-response-sign is canonical base64 of 64 bytes, and the Ed25519 signature verifies over the message rebuilt from verify.request and verify.response: valid.
Otherwise, if it verifies with bodyHash "unread": request_unbound. Otherwise invalid.

reasons.missing: a signature header is absent or empty
reasons.unsupported_version: a signature version this verifier does not know
reasons.invalid: malformed headers or certificate, a certificate valid for more than 3600 seconds, or a signature that does not verify
reasons.unknown_root: the certificate names a root that is not pinned
reasons.expired: ts outside the certificate window, or the verifier clock past notAfter + skew
reasons.request_unbound: authentic, but the gateway did not read the request body, so it is not bound to it

caseFormat.signed: what the gateway signed; certificate is null when the certificate is not canonical (certText is then the exact text the root signed); headers are the four headers it sent
caseFormat.verify: what the verifier gets: the request as the client sent it, the response as received (headers may be altered or stripped), now in Unix seconds, and the names of the pinned roots (keys.roots)
caseFormat.expected: { valid: true } or { valid: false, reason }
caseFormat.bodies: all bodies are base64 of the exact bytes

cases.name: valid_current_root
cases.description: POST creating a deposit address, certificate from the current root.

cases.name: valid_next_root
cases.description: Same response, certificate from the next root (after a root rotation).

cases.name: valid_second_pod_key
cases.description: Another pod: different Ed25519 key and keyId under the same root.

cases.name: valid_unauthenticated_error
cases.description: A 401 sent before API-key validation, to a request without x-api-sign: requestSign is empty.

cases.name: valid_get_with_query
cases.description: GET with a query string and no request body.

cases.name: valid_empty_query
cases.description: GET without a query string: the query field is empty.

cases.name: valid_empty_request_body
cases.description: POST with an empty body: bodyHash is the SHA-256 of zero bytes.

cases.name: valid_head_empty_body
cases.description: HEAD: the response body is empty, so the message ends right after the final newline.

cases.name: valid_204_empty_body
cases.description: DELETE answered 204: empty response body.

cases.name: valid_utf8_body
cases.description: Response body with non-ASCII UTF-8 and a newline: the body is signed as raw bytes.

cases.name: valid_percent_encoded_path
cases.description: Path and query keep their percent-encoding exactly as sent (an encoded slash, space, and UTF-8).

cases.name: valid_mixed_case_header_names
cases.description: Header names are case-insensitive; a verifier must find them in any case.

cases.name: valid_with_keypair_sign
cases.description: A request also signed with the client key pair (Ed25519): keypairSign is its x-api-keypair-sign, 88 characters.

cases.name: valid_with_keypair_sign_der_length
cases.description: A key-pair signature as long as a P-256 DER one: keypairSign is 96 characters.

cases.name: valid_ts_at_not_before
cases.description: ts equals notBefore (inclusive).

cases.name: valid_ts_at_not_after_now_at_skew_limit
cases.description: ts equals notAfter and now equals notAfter + 300 (both inclusive).

cases.name: tampered_response_body
cases.description: The deposit address in the body replaced with another one.

cases.name: tampered_status
cases.description: Status 201 changed to 200.

cases.name: tampered_timestamp
cases.description: x-api-response-timestamp moved by one second, still inside the certificate window.

cases.name: tampered_signature
cases.description: x-api-response-sign replaced by another well-formed 64-byte value.

cases.name: signature_not_canonical_base64
cases.description: x-api-response-sign without its base64 padding.

cases.name: signed_by_other_pod_key
cases.description: The certificate is for pod1, the response was signed with pod2.

cases.name: tampered_request_method
cases.description: Client sent PUT; the gateway signed for POST.

cases.name: tampered_request_path
cases.description: Client sent vault B; the gateway signed for vault A.

cases.name: tampered_request_query
cases.description: Client sent offset=10; the gateway signed for offset=0.

cases.name: tampered_request_body
cases.description: The gateway received a different request body (another label), so the signed bodyHash differs.

cases.name: tampered_body_hash
cases.description: The gateway signed the empty-body hash while the client sent a body (body stripped on the way).

cases.name: tampered_request_sign
cases.description: The x-api-sign the gateway signed differs from the one the client sent.

cases.name: tampered_request_keypair_sign
cases.description: The x-api-keypair-sign the gateway signed differs from the one the client sent.

cases.name: keypair_sign_dropped
cases.description: The client sent x-api-keypair-sign; it was stripped on the way, so the gateway signed an empty keypairSign.

cases.name: keypair_sign_added
cases.description: The client sent no x-api-keypair-sign; one was added on the way, and the gateway signed it.

cases.name: response_for_other_request
cases.description: Response A (create address in vault A) presented as the answer to request B (list addresses in vault B).

cases.name: request_body_unread
cases.description: The gateway did not read the request body (over 1 MB or aborted) and signed bodyHash "unread": authentic, but not bound to the body.

cases.name: expired_certificate
cases.description: Signed after notAfter (a pod keeps signing when renewal fails): ts > notAfter.

cases.name: now_beyond_skew
cases.description: ts inside the window but the verifier clock is notAfter + 301.

cases.name: not_yet_valid
cases.description: ts one second before notBefore.

cases.name: timestamp_leading_zero
cases.description: x-api-response-timestamp with a leading zero is not a canonical decimal.

cases.name: unknown_root
cases.description: A correctly signed certificate from a root that is not pinned.

cases.name: rotated_out_root
cases.description: Certificate from the current root after the client dropped it (pins only next).

cases.name: root_id_swapped
cases.description: The certificate names the next root but was signed by the current one.

cases.name: certificate_validity_extended
cases.description: notAfter raised by a day in the certificate, root signature kept from the original.

cases.name: certificate_lifetime_too_long
cases.description: A certificate valid for 3601 seconds, one more than the most a verifier accepts, correctly signed by the current root: ts and now are inside it.

cases.name: certificate_lifetime_ten_years
cases.description: A certificate valid for ten years, as a root that signed by mistake would give one, used five years after its notBefore: the window alone would accept it, the lifetime rule refuses it.

cases.name: certificate_key_replaced
cases.description: pod2's key put into pod1's certificate, root signature kept, response signed with pod2.

cases.name: cert_trailing_newline
cases.description: A newline after notAfter.

cases.name: cert_five_lines
cases.description: notAfter missing.

cases.name: cert_seven_lines
cases.description: An extra seventh line.

cases.name: cert_crlf_line_endings
cases.description: CRLF line endings.

cases.name: cert_wrong_tag
cases.description: Unknown certificate tag.

cases.name: cert_root_id_uppercase
cases.description: rootId in uppercase hex.

cases.name: cert_root_id_short
cases.description: rootId of 63 characters.

cases.name: cert_key_id_uppercase
cases.description: keyId in uppercase hex.

cases.name: cert_key_id_full_hash
cases.description: keyId is the whole 64-character hash instead of its first 32 characters.

cases.name: cert_key_id_of_other_key
cases.description: keyId of pod2 next to pod1's public key.

cases.name: cert_public_key_unpadded
cases.description: Public key base64 without padding.

cases.name: cert_public_key_loose_bits
cases.description: Public key base64 with a non-zero bit past the data: same bytes, not the canonical spelling.

cases.name: cert_public_key_31_bytes
cases.description: A 31-byte public key with its matching keyId.

cases.name: cert_public_key_33_bytes
cases.description: A 33-byte public key with its matching keyId.

cases.name: cert_not_before_leading_zero
cases.description: notBefore with a leading zero.

cases.name: cert_not_after_plus_sign
cases.description: notAfter with a "+" sign.

cases.name: cert_not_before_negative
cases.description: A negative notBefore.

cases.name: cert_not_after_fraction
cases.description: notAfter with a fraction.

cases.name: cert_not_after_above_2_53
cases.description: notAfter of 2^53, past the largest integer every verifier can hold exactly (2^53 - 1).

cases.name: cert_not_before_fullwidth_digits
cases.description: notBefore in full-width Unicode digits: the certificate is not ASCII.

cases.name: cert_header_no_separator
cases.description: x-api-response-cert holds only the certificate, no root signature.

cases.name: cert_header_three_parts
cases.description: x-api-response-cert with a third "." part.

cases.name: cert_header_certificate_extra_padding
cases.description: The certificate part of x-api-response-cert with a stray "=": lenient decoders give the same bytes, but it is not the canonical spelling.

cases.name: cert_header_empty_root_signature
cases.description: x-api-response-cert ending in "." with no root signature.

cases.name: missing_sign
cases.description: x-api-response-sign stripped.

cases.name: missing_timestamp
cases.description: x-api-response-timestamp stripped.

cases.name: missing_version
cases.description: x-api-response-sign-version stripped.

cases.name: missing_cert
cases.description: x-api-response-cert stripped.

cases.name: missing_all
cases.description: All four headers stripped (what a strict client must refuse).

cases.name: empty_sign_header
cases.description: x-api-response-sign present but empty counts as missing.

cases.name: version_2
cases.description: x-api-response-sign-version "2".

cases.name: version_1_0
cases.description: x-api-response-sign-version "1.0" is not "1".
